Entries.JodiNewBaby: I can't stop looking at %kid1. They're so small. I keep checking that they're still breathing.$6#$b#Is that normal?$s
Entries.JodiSecondBaby: Two now. I'm exhausted and terrified and I wouldn't trade it for anything.$s

Entries.JodiNewBaby: I held %kid1 and cried like a child myself. Happy crying, the best kind.$l#$b#Thank you for giving me this.
Entries.JodiSecondBaby: %kid1 is a big sibling now. I could burst with pride.$l

Entries.Indoor_Day_3: I caught myself picking out baby names this morning. Then I told myself I'm too old for that.$s#$b#...Aren't I?
Entries.Indoor_Night_4: Do you ever think about having a baby, @? I think about it all the time and I'm too scared to ask.$s
Entries.Outdoor_3: I watched Marnie's calves today and thought, what if? Then my back reminded me I'm not twenty anymore.$s
Entries.Good_3: If we ever had a baby, I'd want to do it right this time. I just don't know if I can.$s#$b#I'd want you with me. If you're willing.
Entries.Good_4: I'd be starting over at an age when most people are finished. Sometimes that terrifies me.$s#$e#But then I look at you and I want to try.
Entries.Rainy_Night_4: Rain always reminds me of rocking Vincent to sleep. I miss that.$s#$b#Is it selfish to want it again?

Entries.Indoor_Day_3: I've been daydreaming about baby names again. This time I'm not talking myself out of it.$h
Entries.Indoor_Night_4: Let's have a baby, @. ...Whenever you're ready. I mean it.$l#$e#I just wanted you to know I want it too.
Entries.Outdoor_3: I can picture a little one toddling between the crops, getting dirt on everything.$h#$b#And me chasing after them with a washcloth.
Entries.Good_3: I'm older this time and my back is sorer and I couldn't be less afraid. Because it's you.$l
Entries.Good_4: Sam and Vincent would be wonderful big brothers. Vincent would definitely teach them about spring onions.$h
Entries.Rainy_Night_4: Cuddling in the rain and talking about someone who isn't here yet. I never thought I'd feel this lucky.$l

Entries.Indoor_Day_0: I feel strange this morning. Not bad strange. Just full of questions.$s
Entries.Indoor_Day_1: My back aches, my feet are swollen, and I'm so scared of doing this wrong that I can't sit still.$s
Entries.Indoor_Day_2: I sat down to rest and ended up crying. Hormones, I told myself. I don't think that's all of it.$s
Entries.Indoor_Day_3: What if I'm too old? What if Sam and Vincent feel pushed aside? I keep making lists of everything that could go wrong.$s
Entries.Indoor_Day_4: Please don't tell me I'm glowing. I feel like a swollen watermelon with anxiety.$6#$e#...Thank you for being patient with me.
Entries.Indoor_Night_0: I felt something move today. I didn't know whether to laugh or cry, so I did both.$s
Entries.Indoor_Night_1: Will you stay close tonight? I keep having bad dreams, and your voice is the only thing that stops them.$s
Entries.Indoor_Night_2: I keep picturing myself at three in the morning, alone and exhausted. Then I remember you're here.$s
Entries.Indoor_Night_3: My back is on fire. I'm trying not to complain. ...I'm complaining a little. Sorry.$s
Entries.Indoor_Night_4: Thank you for rubbing my back. I don't know how to say what it means to be taken care of.$s

Entries.Indoor_Day_0: Good morning, love! The baby kicked at sunrise. An early riser, just like you.$h
Entries.Indoor_Day_1: My back hurts and my feet are swollen and I've never been happier. Isn't that funny?$h
Entries.Indoor_Day_2: I've been knitting a tiny blanket. Badly. You didn't see it.$l
Entries.Indoor_Day_3: I told Sam and Vincent. Vincent asked if the baby would like spring onions. Sam just hugged me for a long time.$h
Entries.Indoor_Day_4: I keep catching myself with a hand on my belly, talking to them. I told them about you. They're lucky to have you.$l
Entries.Indoor_Night_0: Come here, feel this! There. Did you feel the kick? That's our baby saying hello.$l
Entries.Indoor_Night_1: I used to be scared of everything. Now I'm only scared of how much I already love them.$l
Entries.Indoor_Night_2: Rub my back, please? I'll pay you in kisses and cookies.$h
Entries.Indoor_Night_3: Whatever happens, we'll figure it out together. I know that now.$l
Entries.Indoor_Night_4: Goodnight, you two. Yes, both of you. I'm talking to the baby as well.$h

Entries.OneKid_0: %kid1 smiled at me today and I nearly cried. A mother of three... who would have thought.$s
Entries.OneKid_1: I'm so tired, but when %kid1 grabs my finger I forget everything else.$s#$e#I'm just afraid I'm doing it wrong.
Entries.OneKid_2: My back is screaming from carrying %kid1 around, but I won't put them down. I'm sorry, I'm clingy.$s
Entries.OneKid_3: Sam wants to meet %kid1 soon. I hope he doesn't feel I've moved on and left him behind.$s
Entries.OneKid_4: Do you think I'm a good mother? Not just to %kid1. To all of them. I keep doubting it.$s

Entries.OneKid_0: %kid1 fell asleep on my chest this morning. I could have stayed there forever.$l
Entries.OneKid_1: My back aches, my eyes are heavy, and I wouldn't change a thing.$h
Entries.OneKid_2: Vincent asked to hold %kid1. He was so careful, like they were made of glass. I got teary.$h
Entries.OneKid_3: Look at %kid1, @. They have your smile. I'm so glad.$l#$e#And my stubbornness, poor thing.$h
Entries.OneKid_4: A second chance at being a mother, with you beside me. I never take it for granted.$l

Entries.TwoKids_0: %kid1 and %kid2 are finally asleep. I'm too tired to be anxious, which is a relief.$s
Entries.TwoKids_1: I read about raising more than one child and spent an hour worrying I'd get everything wrong.$s
Entries.TwoKids_2: My back is giving up on me. %kid1 wants to be carried and %kid2 wants to be carried. I'm outnumbered.$s
Entries.TwoKids_3: Sometimes I count my kids and the number surprises me. Four. I still feel like someone who got lost.$s#$e#But I'm here. I'm trying.
Entries.TwoKids_4: Thank you for staying. For %kid1, for %kid2, for me. I'm scared every day that you won't, and you keep showing up.$s

Entries.TwoKids_0: The house is quiet, %kid1 and %kid2 are asleep, and I'm leaning on the one I love. I'm happy.$l
Entries.TwoKids_1: Perhaps I could ask Sam to babysit %kid1 and %kid2 so we can have a quiet dinner. I'd miss them within the hour.$h
Entries.TwoKids_2: I used to think a big family was too much. Now I can't imagine our house any other way.$l
Entries.TwoKids_3: My back says four kids is a lot. My heart says it's perfect.$h
Entries.TwoKids_4: Look at them playing together. We did that.$l#$e#I'm so proud, @.
